_about: Curated articulation guidance used to ground feedback (General American English). Plain-language descriptions of standard articulatory phonetics; reviewed wording should be confirmed by a speech-language pathologist before clinical use.

p.label: p as in 'pen'
p.how: Press your lips together, build up a little air, then pop them open. No voice.

b.label: b as in 'bat'
b.how: Press your lips together and open them with your voice on (feel a buzz in your throat).

t.label: t as in 'top'
t.how: Touch the tip of your tongue to the bumpy ridge just behind your top front teeth, then release a quick puff of air.

d.label: d as in 'dog'
d.how: Tongue tip on the ridge behind your top front teeth, then release with your voice on.

k.label: k as in 'cat'
k.how: Lift the back of your tongue against the soft back part of the roof of your mouth, keep the tongue tip down, then release a puff of air.

ɡ.label: g as in 'go'
ɡ.how: Back of the tongue up against the back of the roof of your mouth, tongue tip down, release with your voice on.

f.label: f as in 'fan'
f.how: Rest your top front teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow air out steadily.

v.label: v as in 'van'
v.how: Top teeth lightly on your bottom lip, blow air and keep your voice buzzing.

θ.label: voiceless 'th' as in 'thumb'
θ.how: Put the tip of your tongue lightly between or just behind your top front teeth and blow air gently. No voice.

ð.label: voiced 'th' as in 'this'
ð.how: Tongue tip lightly between or just behind your top teeth, blow air and keep your voice buzzing.

s.label: s as in 'sun'
s.how: Keep your teeth close together and your tongue tip just behind (not touching) your top teeth. Blow a thin, steady stream of air for a clear hiss.

z.label: z as in 'zoo'
z.how: Same tongue position as /s/, but turn your voice on so it buzzes like a bee.

ʃ.label: sh as in 'shoe'
ʃ.how: Pull your tongue a little further back than for /s/, round and push your lips forward, and blow a soft 'shhh'.

ʒ.label: the 'zh' sound in 'measure'
ʒ.how: Same position as 'sh', with your voice turned on.

h.label: h as in 'hat'
h.how: Open your mouth and breathe out gently, like fogging up a window.

tʃ.label: ch as in 'chair'
tʃ.how: Start with your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth (like /t/), then release it straight into 'sh' with rounded lips.

dʒ.label: j as in 'jump'
dʒ.how: Start like /d/ with your tongue tip on the ridge, then release into the 'zh' sound with your voice on and lips rounded.

m.label: m as in 'moon'
m.how: Close your lips and hum, letting the sound come out through your nose.

n.label: n as in 'nose'
n.how: Touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth and hum through your nose.

ŋ.label: the 'ng' sound in 'sing'
ŋ.how: Lift the back of your tongue against the back of the roof of your mouth and hum through your nose. Don't add a /g/ at the end.

l.label: l as in 'leaf'
l.how: Touch the tip of your tongue to the ridge behind your top front teeth and let your voice flow around the sides of your tongue. Keep your lips relaxed.

r.label: r as in 'red'
r.how: Lift or bunch your tongue toward the roof of your mouth without touching it, with the sides of your tongue against your upper back teeth. Lips only slightly rounded.

w.label: w as in 'web'
w.how: Round your lips into a small circle, then open them as you move into the vowel.

j.label: y as in 'yes'
j.how: Raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth as for 'ee', then glide into the vowel.

i.label: the 'ee' vowel in 'see'
i.how: Spread your lips slightly as in a smile, with your tongue high and forward.

ɪ.label: the short 'i' vowel in 'sit'
ɪ.how: Like 'ee' but more relaxed and shorter; the tongue is a little lower.

eɪ.label: the 'ay' vowel in 'cake'
eɪ.how: Start with a mid 'eh' and glide up toward 'ee'.

ɛ.label: the 'e' vowel in 'bed'
ɛ.how: Open your jaw a little, tongue forward and in the middle, lips relaxed.

æ.label: the 'a' vowel in 'cat'
æ.how: Drop your jaw wide open, keep your tongue low and forward, lips spread slightly.

ɑ.label: the 'ah' vowel in 'father'
ɑ.how: Open your jaw wide with your tongue low and toward the back, lips relaxed.

ɔ.label: the 'aw' vowel in 'thought'
ɔ.how: Open your jaw and round your lips slightly, tongue low and back.

oʊ.label: the 'oh' vowel in 'go'
oʊ.how: Start with rounded lips and glide toward an even smaller 'oo' circle.

ʊ.label: the short 'oo' vowel in 'book'
ʊ.how: Lips loosely rounded, tongue high and back, short and relaxed.

u.label: the long 'oo' vowel in 'moon'
u.how: Round your lips into a small tight circle with your tongue high and back.

ʌ.label: the 'u' vowel in 'cup'
ʌ.how: Relax your mouth, open your jaw slightly and say a short 'uh'.

ə.label: the quick unstressed 'uh' (as in the first syllable of 'banana')
ə.how: A very short, relaxed 'uh' with no effort. Don't stretch it.

ɜr.label: the 'er' vowel in 'bird'
ɜr.how: Bunch your tongue up and back as for /r/, keep your lips slightly rounded, and hold the 'er' sound.

ər.label: the unstressed 'er' at the end of 'butter'
ər.how: A short 'er' sound: tongue bunched as for /r/, said quickly.

aɪ.label: the 'eye' vowel in 'five'
aɪ.how: Start with an open 'ah' and glide smoothly up toward 'ee'.

aʊ.label: the 'ow' vowel in 'house'
aʊ.how: Start with an open 'ah' and glide into 'oo', rounding your lips as you go.

ɔɪ.label: the 'oy' vowel in 'boy'
ɔɪ.how: Start with a rounded 'aw' and glide up toward 'ee'.

contrasts.r>w: For /r/ keep your lips more relaxed instead of rounding them, and let your tongue do the work: lift or bunch it so the sides touch your upper back teeth.
contrasts.r>l: For /r/ the tongue tip should not touch the roof of your mouth; pull it back slightly so it floats.
contrasts.l>w: For /l/ touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth, and don't round your lips.
contrasts.l>j: For /l/ use the tongue tip on the ridge, rather than raising the middle of the tongue.
contrasts.s>θ: Keep your tongue tip behind your teeth for /s/, not between them, so the air makes a sharp hiss.
contrasts.s>ʃ: For /s/ move your tongue tip slightly forward and keep your lips relaxed instead of rounded.
contrasts.s>t: Keep the air flowing for /s/ instead of stopping it.
contrasts.z>s: Turn your voice on for /z/: put a hand on your throat and feel it buzz.
contrasts.z>ð: Keep your tongue tip behind your teeth for /z/.
contrasts.θ>f: Use your tongue, not your lip: put the tongue tip lightly between your teeth for 'th'.
contrasts.θ>t: Let the air keep flowing for 'th' instead of stopping it with your tongue.
contrasts.θ>s: Bring your tongue tip forward to touch your top teeth for 'th'.
contrasts.ð>d: Let the air and voice flow for 'th' (as in 'this') instead of stopping them.
contrasts.ð>v: Use your tongue tip against your teeth for 'th', not your lip.
contrasts.ð>z: Bring your tongue tip forward to your teeth for 'th'.
contrasts.ʃ>s: For 'sh' pull your tongue slightly back and push your lips forward into a round shape.
contrasts.tʃ>ʃ: Start 'ch' with a short stop: tongue tip on the ridge first, then release into 'sh'.
contrasts.tʃ>t: After the /t/-like start, release into a 'sh' sound for 'ch'.
contrasts.dʒ>d: After the /d/-like start, release into a buzzing 'zh' sound for 'j'.
contrasts.k>t: Use the back of your tongue for /k/: keep the tip down behind your bottom teeth.
contrasts.ɡ>d: Use the back of your tongue for /g/: keep the tip down behind your bottom teeth.
contrasts.t>k: Use the tip of your tongue for /t/, on the ridge behind your top teeth.
contrasts.d>ɡ: Use the tip of your tongue for /d/, on the ridge behind your top teeth.
contrasts.f>p: Keep the air flowing for /f/: teeth on lip, don't close your lips.
contrasts.v>b: Teeth on your bottom lip for /v/ and keep the buzz going.
contrasts.b>p: Add your voice for /b/: feel your throat buzz as your lips open.
contrasts.p>b: Make /p/ without voice: just a puff of air.
contrasts.t>d: Make /t/ with a clear puff of air and no voice.
contrasts.k>ɡ: Make /k/ with a clear puff of air and no voice.
contrasts.n>m: For /n/ keep your lips apart and use your tongue tip on the ridge.
contrasts.ŋ>n: For 'ng' use the back of your tongue, not the tip.

patterns.deletion_final: Make sure you finish the word: say the last sound clearly before you stop.
patterns.deletion_cluster: Say the cluster slowly first, holding the first sound, then join them together.
patterns.deletion_initial: Start the word with its first sound: try saying that sound alone, then add the rest.
patterns.syllable_missing: Clap or tap once for each syllable while you say the word slowly, then speed up.
patterns.extra_syllable: Join the consonants together without adding a little 'uh' between them.
patterns.too_fast: Slow down a little and give every sound its time.
patterns.too_slow: Once the word feels comfortable, try saying it at a natural pace.
patterns.unclear_vowel: Listen to the example and copy the mouth shape for the vowel; hold it a little longer.
patterns.low_acoustic_similarity: Listen to the example again and try to match its rhythm and melody.
patterns.part_mismatch: Listen to that part of the example, say it slowly on its own a few times, then say the whole word.
patterns.stress_pattern: Make the stressed syllable a little louder and longer, like in the example.
patterns.pitch_pattern: Listen to how the example's voice rises and falls, then copy that melody.
